skill.name: chapter-outline-generator
skill.description: Creates structured book chapter outlines with chapter summaries, learning objectives, sections, subsections, and estimated word counts.
skill.summary: Plan fiction and nonfiction book chapters with clear structure, flow, and word count guidance.
skill.author: AbdulSamad94

content.value_statement: Writers often struggle to turn a book idea into balanced chapters. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create chapter plans with objectives, sections, subsections, and word counts.
actual_capabilities: Collects book title, genre, audience, theme, length, and chapter count before outlining.
Creates chapter titles, summaries, learning objectives, major sections, and subsections.
Estimates word counts based on book length and chapter importance.
Checks chapter order for logical progression and topic coverage.
Supports fiction, nonfiction, business, academic, and general reader book plans.
Provides a validation checklist for reviewing the final outline.
limitations: Does not write full manuscript chapters from the outline.
Does not verify factual claims or source citations for nonfiction books.
Needs user-provided book context for accurate structure and pacing.
May require revision for publisher-specific formatting or editorial standards.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Nonfiction Book
use_cases.description: Create a full chapter framework for a business, education, self-help, or research-based book.

use_cases.title: Structure Early Fiction Chapters
use_cases.description: Outline opening chapters with plot movement, character setup, scene groups, and estimated length.

use_cases.title: Rebalance an Existing Draft
use_cases.description: Review chapter purposes, section coverage, and word count distribution to improve flow.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a Simple Book Idea
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with basic book details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chapter-outline-generator skill to outline a book titled [title]. The genre is [genre], the audience is [audience], and I want [number] chapters.

prompt_templates.title: Expand One Chapter
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop one chapter into sections and subsections.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chapter-outline-generator skill to expand Chapter [number], titled [chapter title]. Include a summary, objectives, sections, subsections, and an estimated word count.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Nonfiction Table of Contents
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a complete plan for an instructional or business book.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chapter-outline-generator skill to create a table of contents for a nonfiction book about [topic]. Target [audience], use [total word count] words, and include learning objectives for each chapter.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Rebalance a Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chapter-outline-generator skill to review this draft outline: [paste outline]. Identify missing topics, weak progression, chapter imbalance, and suggest a revised structure.

output_examples.input: A first-time founder wants a 10 chapter book about managing remote teams.
output: Chapter 1 introduces the shift to remote work and why office-based habits fail online.
Sections cover adoption trends, common management mistakes, and the remote leadership mindset.
The chapter includes three learning objectives and an estimated 4,000 word target.

output_examples.input: A mystery novelist needs the first three chapters for an art theft story.
output: Chapter 1 opens with the detective receiving a late call about missing paintings.
Chapter 2 develops the crime scene, witness interviews, and early contradictions.
Chapter 3 introduces suspects and ends with a clue that changes the investigation.

output_examples.input: An editor wants to rebalance an uneven self-help outline.
output: The revised structure groups repeated mindset topics into one chapter.
Practical exercises move later, after the reader understands the core framework.
Word counts are redistributed so introductory chapters stay shorter.

best_practices: Provide the target reader, genre, book goal, and desired length before asking for an outline.
Review the full outline for progression before approving individual chapter details.
Use estimated word counts as planning guides, then adjust after drafting.
anti_patterns: Do not request a complete manuscript when you only need chapter planning.
Do not omit audience and genre details for books with specialized reader needs.
Do not accept the first outline without checking topic gaps and repeated sections.

faq.question: Can this skill create a full book outline?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a chapter-by-chapter structure with summaries, objectives, sections, subsections, and word counts.

faq.question: Does it work for fiction and nonfiction?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover both mystery fiction and nonfiction business writing.

faq.question: Can it create a table of contents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce a structured table of contents and expand each chapter into detailed parts.

faq.question: Does it write the chapters?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on planning chapter structure, not drafting full manuscript text.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the title, genre, audience, theme, target length, and preferred chapter count when available.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing outline?
faq.answer: Yes. It can check flow, balance, missing topics, and word count distribution.
